walkthrough: Goal: stage 3 (V大's 点定位): learn to place points by eye, first on the flat (a point in its frame, a proportion along a segment, an angle) with exact answers, then in space on a box by V大's five tricks; see the exact answer and the way to see it after each try, never a score.

Entry (S101: the test crops imported first, so a combination copies a crop): lessons from the home. Estimates at level 1 lays six points, at level 2 proportions and points mixed (a proportion first), at level 3 angles and proportions (an angle first); Points in space at level 1 the centre and the halves, at level 2 the thirds and the next face, at level 3 the mirror and one of the others. Between them Home leaves a lesson under way, or Finish and That's all for today end it.

A point: the left frame holds a dot; the empty frame beside it is mine. The first time, the instructions show by themselves: mark where the dot lies, judged by the frame (never a grid), against the half and then the thirds, again and again; with Draw, a dot or a small cross, the last mark counting; Sketch for my own guides. The tools beside the frame: Sketch, Draw, Undo, Redo, nothing else. I put a dot a little right of and above where it should be.

Compare: the exact point is a red cross over my frame, as thick as my pen and see-through; the point read from my dot is ringed blue. Dashed pencil runs the point across and down to both frames' edges, and both frames' top and left edges are ticked at the half and the thirds, so I see where it really sits: a bit past a third across, a bit past the half down. The card is only its title (the How said what the marks mean). The pen is blue: I make a small cross on the red one, Compare again: the blue ring is on the red cross, the correction read in place of my dot. The record keeps my first error, across and down, for later; no number is shown.

A proportion: the left frame holds a segment with a dot dividing it; mine holds a segment turned and longer or shorter; in both the end the share counts from is ringed, the other barred. I tick my segment a little past its third (wrong: the dot sits at the half). Compare: the exact place is a red bar across my segment, my tick ringed blue; both segments' halves and thirds are ticked in pencil, so the dot reads as the half. A dot in blue on the red bar, Compare: ringed on it.

An angle: the left frame holds a line, mine a dot. I draw through the dot ten degrees too flat. Compare: the exact line red through the dot, mine dashed blue run on to my frame's edges, where the miss is plain; pencil runs the original's line on to its frame's edges and an upright cross sits through each line's middle. I redraw it in blue along the red; Compare: the blue dashes lie on it.

Points in space: a lesson of Points in space at level 1: a box in two-point perspective in ink in both frames as the eye sees it (no hidden edges across the face), its horizon labelled, one front face shaded in pencil. The centre's instructions: in perspective the centre lies nearer the far edge; cross the face's diagonals with Sketch; mark it with Draw, every point with a reason. I draw the diagonals with Sketch but mark the middle of the drawing with Draw (wrong). Compare: the exact centre red, my dot ringed blue a little nearer the front; the left box now shows the diagonals in dashed pencil and the centre in ink, kept inside its frame. A blue cross where my diagonals cross; Compare: ringed on the red.

The halves: halve the face with a line towards its vanishing point. I draw it tilted (wrong: it should run to the vanishing point, here near level). Compare: the exact line red, mine dashed blue crossing it; the left box shows the diagonals, the line through the centre to the vanishing point. Corrected along the red.
Finish ends the lesson: Points in space, 2 exercises, a dot each; That's all for today. A lesson of Points in space at level 2 opens on the thirds, on the same box.

The thirds: two uprights at equal depths. I put them at the drawing's equal thirds (wrong: the near third is longer). Compare: the exact uprights red a little farther back, mine dashed blue; the left box shows the near edge's thirds run to the vanishing point and the diagonal crossing them where the uprights stand. Corrected in blue.

Chinese: Next, then All tools, Actions, 中文, back: the next face's instructions in Chinese (等距扩展): halve the far edge by the line from the near edge's middle to the vanishing point; a line from the near top corner through that middle meets the bottom edge, run on, at the next face's far corner. With Sketch the line to the vanishing point, the bottom edge run on and the diagonal; with Draw the upright, but where the picture's equal width would put it (wrong). Compare: the next face red (its far upright, top and bottom edges), my upright dashed blue too far; the left box shows the construction. Corrected on the red. Finish; That's all for today.

The mirror (对称点), a lesson of Points in space at level 3, its first: a dot on the face, mirror it across the face's upright middle. I mirror it in the drawing's middle (wrong). Compare: the exact mirror red, mine ringed blue; the left box shows the diagonals, the upright middle, the dot's level to the vanishing point, the rectangle between the dot and the middle with its diagonals, the half height and the diagonal down to the mirror's foot. A blue cross on the red; Compare: ringed on it. Next, Finish.

Undo: every mark and correction is a stroke on the sheet, undone and redone as any; the comparison is the screen's, never the artwork's. Reopened, the sheet and its records are as left; the record of each first Compare keeps its error for the trajectories.
Not here: the solids drawn (s93-solids); on the tablet's own hand (the author's).
